episode_title: Do Most Retirees Gain or Lose Weight After Retirement?

real_qa.q: Do most retirees gain or lose weight after retirement according to peer-reviewed research?
real_qa.r: A peer-reviewed research report from the Journals of Gerontology found there was no relationship between retirement and weight change for men. For women, there was also no relationship except for a subset of women who were normal weight before retirement and worked blue collar jobs. Professional services workers showed no relationship between retirement and weight change.
real_qa.requete: retirement weight gain loss research study

real_qa.q: What percentage of retirees lost weight after retirement according to the Big Picture Retirement Show YouTube poll?
real_qa.r: In a YouTube poll asking what happened to weight after retirement, 36 percent said they lost at least 10 pounds, which was the largest result. 23 percent said they gained 10 pounds, and 34 percent stayed within 10 pounds. There was also a small number that fluctuated all over the board.
real_qa.requete: Big Picture Retirement YouTube poll weight loss retirement

real_qa.q: Why do desk job workers often gain weight when they retire?
real_qa.r: For people who work desk jobs like the host, retirement often leads to increased movement and weight loss since they are no longer sitting at a desk all day. However, the opposite occurs for people in physically active jobs: an airline mechanic commented he walked more than two miles daily in his maintenance facility, and after retirement began sitting more and gained weight.
real_qa.requete: desk job retirement weight gain physical activity

real_qa.q: How many steps per day was the host getting while working at his office desk job?
real_qa.r: When the host tracked his step count during a week in the office with no exercise, working 8 to 10 hours at the office, going home, eating dinner, doing chores, and then working on his computer until bedtime, he averaged only about 1,800 steps per day.
real_qa.requete: desk job daily steps sedentary work

real_qa.q: What does research show about the relationship between retirement health and overall retirement happiness?
real_qa.r: A Fidelity study found that retirees who reported good health also reported much higher marks in other areas of retirement happiness. Those who reported bad health reported lower satisfaction in other areas, indicating that health impacts nearly all aspects of retirement satisfaction.

guest.bio_context: John K. Ross is a co-host of the Big Picture Retirement Show. He is described by the host as notably fit and physically active, maintaining a rigorous fitness routine including early morning gym visits at 5 a.m. on weekdays and weekends. He lives in Hot Springs and Texarkana, and follows a disciplined approach to nutrition and exercise habits.
